conviction_note: Near-balanced: the share-count arithmetic (Q3 weighted diluted ~22.2-22.4M vs 25.2M a year ago) and a firm used-retail backdrop (Cox: Sept used retail sales +2% y/y, listings +6% y/y, credit availability best since 2015; CarMax comps +13%) lean slightly positive, offset by accelerated late-quarter wholesale depreciation, flat industry new sales with Detroit-3 share at a record low, the Sept 16 Fed hike and a sharp slowdown in Q3 buybacks; the bar is disputed ($9.30-$10.09), so p_up is held at 51 on an abs move of 6.0 (event-implied 5.42%, own median 4.96%, last print +19.3%), and impact_sum (-0.3) and impact_scaled (+0.12) agree on 'about zero'.
bar: Disputed. Adjusted EPS consensus: $9.73 on 5 estimates (therighttrader/unusualwhales aggregator, https://therighttrader.com/earnings-calendar/lad), $9.85 (Earnings Whispers, https://beta.earningswhispers.com/go/w/LAD), $10.09 / revenue $9.81B (Benzinga KR, https://kr.benzinga.com/quote/LAD/earnings-forecasts), single-analyst Zacks $9.30 (https://www.marketbeat.com/instant-alerts/zacks-research-boosts-earnings-estimates-for-lithia-motors-2026-03-30/). Revenue bar ~$9.7-9.8B. No company guidance (the Q2 release gives no numeric outlook: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001023128/000102312826000047/a2026q2exx99earningsrelease.htm). Sized against ~$9.9 midpoint; no two sources agree, so every finding is capped small. Year-ago comp: adj EPS $9.50, adj NI $240.9M on 25.2M diluted shares (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1023128/000102312825000123/a2025q3exx99earningsrelease.htm).
positioning_check: Short interest 1,941,871 shares at the 2026-09-30 settlement, 5.02 days to cover (equibles, https://equibles.com/stocks/lad/short-interest), ~8% of shares outstanding (not float-adjusted); down from 2,752,956 (10.8 DTC) at 2026-06-15 and 2,588,008 at 2026-07-15, so shorts covered into and after the +19.3% Q2 print and the subsequent ~30% drawdown; not a crowded short. Borrow fee 0.4% (curvedtrading, July). Skew +0.48 vol points (balanced, baseline), put/call OI 2.12 on a tiny 1,714 contracts, ATM spread 14.7% of mid. Stock -30.6% from 52w high, -16.8% since the last print (https://unusualwhales.com/stock/LAD/earnings, as of 2026-10-20), -4.96% over 20d, +3.5% over 5d. findings.finding: Share-count arithmetic favours a modest EPS beat: Q2 2026 adjusted NI was $227.6M on ~22.7M weighted diluted shares ($10.03); with only ~108k shares bought in Q3 through Sept 8 after 854k in Q2, Q3 weighted diluted shares should be ~22.2-22.4M versus 25.2M in Q3 2025 (-11%), so merely repeating Q2's adjusted NI gives ~$10.15-10.25 against a $9.73-$10.09 bar; the y/y line comps are also easier than Q2's (Q3 2025 same-store used GPU $1,767 vs Q2 2026 $2,019; new GPU $2,867 vs $2,718, so the new-GPU decline narrows from -11% to ~-5%; DFC income $19.1M vs $36.5M in Q2 2026), while seasonally Q3 2025 NI ($240.9M) matched Q2 2025 (~$242M).
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026 adjusted EPS $10.03 vs ~$8.7-8.9 consensus (+13-15%) bought +19.3% on the day; Q1 2026 +4.96%; Q3 2025 beat ($9.50 vs ~$8.5-9.1) moved -1.13%; 3 of 7 prints up. The name pays for a large EPS beat but a small one has gone either way.
findings.why_not_priced: Consensus has risen to ~$9.7-10.1 after the Q2 beat, so most of this is modelled; the residual is that the top of the range only equals a flat-sequential quarter. If the market believed a ~$10.2+ print were base case, the stock would not sit 17% below the post-Q2 level with estimates spread from $9.30 to $10.09.
findings.independence: Same company documents as the Q3 2025 comp (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1023128/000102312825000123/a2025q3exx99earningsrelease.htm) and the Sept 8 buyback update (https://investors.lithiadriveway.com/press-releases/mtsh0nbwidd7x9cm1zf); management's Q2 call said June SG&A was 'the exit rate we wanted' and used volume 'flat to up mid-single digits' in H2 (https://quartr.com/events/lithia-motors-inc-lad-q2-2026_ozHXG8iA). All company-sourced, one line of argument.

findings.finding: Industry used-retail backdrop in Q3 was firm: Cox (published 2026-10-16) puts September used retail sales +2% y/y, average listing price $27,235 (+~6% y/y, highest since Dec 2022) and the Dealertrack credit availability index at its highest since April 2015, while Manheim wholesale prices were -1.2% y/y unadjusted; a retail/wholesale spread widening plus easier credit supports LAD used volumes, used GPU, F&I and DFC originations (used retail ~36% of revenue).
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026 used GPU +$339 sequentially was a cited driver of the +19.3% day; Q2 2025 used softness accompanied -5.63%. Used is the line this stock has traded on.
findings.why_not_priced: Published four days before the print, after most previews; the stock has fallen ~17% since July on rates and auto-retail sentiment, which is not what one would see if a firm used-retail quarter were priced. Still an industry proxy, not LAD's own number.
findings.independence: CarMax (direct used-retail peer, reported 2026-09-29, after LAD last spoke): comparable used units +13.0%, wholesale units +15.9%, though retail GPU fell $111 on pricing actions (https://secure.businesswire.com/news/home/20260929484228/en/CarMax-Reports-Second-Quarter-Fiscal-2027-Results). Cox also raised its 2026 used retail forecast to 20.5M from 20.4M (https://www.coxautoinc.com/press-releases/q3-2026-muvvi-press-release/). Proxy evidence.

findings.finding: Wholesale depreciation accelerated late in Q3: the Manheim index fell 1.1% m/m in September (seasonal norm +0.3%), unadjusted -1.3% m/m vs a -0.3% norm, three-year-old MMR -1.7% vs typical -1.5%, sales conversion 1.9 pts below the 3-year September average, and Cox cut its 2026 year-end Manheim forecast from +2% (July) to +0.2%, citing higher fuel costs and rapidly climbing rates; faster depreciation pressures used GPU on inventory bought earlier in the quarter, the line that drove LAD's Q2.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Used GPU swings have been the swing factor (Q2 2026 +$339 sequential = +19.3% day). No cited instance of a depreciation-driven used GPU miss in the 7-print history.
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced: the sector sold off in September. But consensus moved up after Q2 (to $9.7-10.1) and has not visibly been cut for late-quarter depreciation; if it had, the top estimates would sit below Q2's $10.03.
findings.independence: Cox Q3 MUVVI release (https://www.coxautoinc.com/press-releases/q3-2026-muvvi-press-release/), same publisher; CarMax wholesale GPU -$135 y/y (https://secure.businesswire.com/news/home/20260929484228/en/CarMax-Reports-Second-Quarter-Fiscal-2027-Results). Offsets part of the previous finding (retail held while wholesale fell).

findings.finding: New-vehicle volume was flat-to-down in Q3: industry Q3 sales -0.4% (CarPro), Cox projected Q3 at 4.12M (below Q2 and a year ago) with September SAAR ~16.3M vs 16.6M a year ago and the Detroit 3 at their lowest share on record (GM -6%, Stellantis flat at 324,277); LAD same-store new units were already -2.2% in Q2 with new GPU 'stabilized' at $2,718.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: New GPU compression (-11% y/y in Q2) did not stop a +19.3% day; new has not been the line LAD trades on recently.
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced; industry volumes are public and in every model. Residual is the Detroit-3 share loss against LAD's domestic-brand exposure, which no preview quantifies.
findings.independence: CarPro Q3 tally (https://www.carpro.com/blog/national-sales-results-for-all-automakers-year-to-date-q3-2026); Stellantis flat Q3 (https://moparinsiders.com/stellantis-u-s-q3-2026-sales-stay-flat-as-ram-surges/). Proxy, not LAD's own units.

findings.finding: UK new-car registrations rose 12.1% y/y in September 2026 to ~350,500, the best September since 2017 and the tenth straight month of growth; LAD's UK (Pendragon) was 18.7% of Q2 revenue and 14.8% of gross profit, with Q2 UK new units +16% and adjusted pretax +78%.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: UK strength was cited in the Q2 call alongside the +19.3% day; no isolated UK-driven reaction on record.
findings.why_not_priced: US analysts rarely model UK plate-change months; September is the UK's second-largest month. Net of the rest: the UK is ~15% of gross profit, and growth is BEV- and Chinese-brand-led (Jaecoo 7 the top seller), which may carry lower margins, so it is sized small.
findings.independence: EY UK commentary (https://www.ey.com/en_uk/newsroom/2026/10/uk-new-car-registrations-continue-growth-in-september); Q2 call UK figures (https://www.webull.com/news/15364343890912256).

findings.finding: The Fed raised rates 25bp on 2026-09-16 (first hike since 2023, more expected) and Cox describes rates as 'climbing rapidly'; LAD fell 5.2% on 2026-09-17 on auto-retail sentiment; higher floorplan and variable debt cost (net debt/adj EBITDA 3.17x, up from 2.53x) and affordability are likely call topics for Q4 commentary, though only two weeks of the hike fall in Q3.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: LAD gives no numeric guidance; call tone has mattered (Q2 'momentum into H2' with +19.3%). No prior rate-hike quarter in the 7-print sample.
findings.why_not_priced: Largely priced: the stock already dropped 5.2% the day after the hike and is -17% since July. The residual is whether management quantifies floorplan/DFC funding cost pressure on the call.
findings.independence: Quiver Quant on the 2026-09-17 drop (https://www.quiverquant.com/news/Lithia+Motors+Falls+as+Auto+Retail+Sentiment+Softens); leverage from the Q2 release (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001023128/000102312826000047/a2026q2exx99earningsrelease.htm).

findings.finding: Q3 buybacks slowed sharply: through the 2026-09-08 update LAD had bought only ~108k shares ($40M at $375 average, 0.46% of shares) in the quarter, against 854k shares ($242M at $284) in Q2, with leverage up to 3.17x net debt/EBITDA and $580M authorization left; management had said roughly a third of capital would go to buybacks.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2's heavy buyback and 23% dividend raise accompanied the +19.3% day; no earlier reaction isolated to capital return.
findings.why_not_priced: The Q3 number has not been aggregated anywhere; the full-quarter figure arrives with the print. If the market had read it as a balance-sheet constraint, leverage would be in previews. Unknown whether buying resumed at ~$300 in late September, which would flip the sign; the price-sensitive pattern (bought at $284, slowed at $375) is equally consistent with value discipline, so it is sized small.
findings.independence: Leverage figures from the Q2 release (same issuer); the Rockwall Hyundai acquisition was funded from balance sheet (same Sept 8 release). Not independent.

findings.finding: Insider selling with no buys: four open-market sells and zero purchases in six months, including CAO David Stork (320 shares, ~$120k, filed 2026-09-10), Richard Bailey (297 shares) and Stacy Loretz-Congdon (150 shares); all small.
findings.why_not_priced: Trivial sizes; public Form 4s. Included for breadth only.

baseline_tension: The evidence is near-balanced, which is consistent with a balanced skew (+0.48) and a stock that has already de-rated ~30% from its high; the mild positive lean from share-count arithmetic cuts slightly against the negative 20-day run-up, but the bar is too disputed to push p_up off 51.
lessons_applied: Rule 6 (bar disputed, $9.30-$10.09 across four sources, no company guide): capped the EPS-arithmetic finding from +0.8 to +0.6 and moved p_up from 52 to 51.
Rule 9 (segment net of the rest): UK finding trimmed from +0.4 to +0.3 because the UK is ~15% of gross profit and its growth is BEV/Chinese-brand led.
Rule 7: short interest checked (1.94M shares, 5.0 DTC, falling), not a crowded short, so the negatives were left at their size.
Rule 1: the name paid +19.3% for a large Q2 beat, so the reaction function does not veto a beat; left the used and EPS findings standing.
Rule 5: used-retail and depreciation findings rest on broad Cox/Manheim series plus a direct peer (CarMax), filed small as proxies; nothing dropped.
